html:
The Leks, or Lakz, were the Lezgian-speaking peoples of southern Dagestan, in the eastern Caucasus, and the name of their medieval principality. They are shown here in 1100.

Arab geographers of the 10th century describe Lakz as a mountain land north of Shirvan and west of Derbent, with its own rulers. Its people were partly Muslim and partly followers of older faiths; Islam spread there slowly from Derbent. Lakz often fought or allied with the Shirvanshahs and the emirs of Derbent. It may be linked to the ancient tribes of Caucasian Albania. Their descendants include today's Lezgins.
